title: Kenyan Fish Fingers
community: Popular in urban Kenyan households — a family favourite
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Fish Fingers — tilapia or other white fish cut into strips, seasoned with Kenyan spices, coated in spiced breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until golden and crispy. Beloved by children and adults alike — the Kenyan take on a universal classic.
longDesc: Fish fingers with a Kenyan twist — the familiar breadcrumbed format elevated with garlic, ginger, lemon, and paprika in the coating. Crispy outside, tender and flaky within, they are the ideal introduction to fish for children and a beloved quick meal for the whole family.
ingredients: 600g tilapia or white fish fillets — cut into finger-sized strips
steps: Mix garlic, lemon juice, paprika, cumin, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Toss the fish strips in this seasoning.
Mix the paprika and cumin into the breadcrumbs for a flavoured coating.
Set up a coating station: flour in bowl 1, beaten egg in bowl 2, spiced breadcrumbs in bowl 3.
Coat each fish strip: flour first, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Press gently to adhere.
Fry in batches for 3—4 minutes until deep golden brown, turning once.
Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately.
chefTips: Season the breadcrumbs as well as the fish — this doubles the flavour impact.
Press the breadcrumbs firmly onto the fish — loose coating falls off during frying.
Make sure the oil is hot enough before the fish goes in.
commonMistakes: Wet fish — pat completely dry before coating or the crumb does not adhere.
Too cool oil — produces soggy, pale fish fingers.

faqs.q: Can I bake these instead of frying?
faqs.a: Yes — place on a lightly oiled baking tray and bake at 200°C for 15—18 minutes, turning halfway. They will not be as crispy as fried but are a lighter option.

cookingScience: The three-stage coating (flour → egg → breadcrumb) creates a moisture barrier that protects the fish during frying. The flour helps the egg adhere; the egg binds the breadcrumbs; the breadcrumbs create the crispy shell through starch gelatinisation and Maillard browning.
sustainabilityTips: Homemade fish fingers produce no excess packaging and allow you to use any sustainable fish variety.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Freeze uncooked for up to 2 months.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 190°C for 8 minutes.
healthBenefits: Homemade version allows control over ingredients.
culturalNote: Fish fingers have become a firm favourite in Kenyan urban households — the familiar format with a distinctly Kenyan spice profile makes them irresistible to children and adults alike.
regionalVariations: Coconut breadcrumb fish fingers — coastal style.
